title: Glossary
markdown:
| Word | Meaning | Lesson |
|---|---|---|
| **__call** | The metamethod that lets a table be called like a function (8.04) |
| **__gc** | A metamethod that runs when the garbage collector frees a table. (7.02) |
| **_ENV** | The table a chunk's free names are looked up in; normally the same as `_G`. (7.01) |
| **%q** | The string.format directive that writes a string as Lua source (8.03) |
| **Anchor** | `^` or `$` in a pattern: the match must start at the beginning or end at the end of the text | 4.02 |
| **Anonymous function** | A function written without a name, `function(x) ... end`, usually passed straight to another function | 3.03 |
| **Base case** | The case where a recursive function stops calling itself | 3.04 |
| **Binary heap** | A priority queue in a list where the children of position i are 2i and 2i + 1 (8.01) |
| **Bitwise operator** | `&`, `|`, `~`, `<<`, `>>` and unary `~`, working on the bits of integers. (7.03) |
| **Block** | A run of statements with its own locals: a function body, a loop body, `then ... end`, `do ... end` | 3.05 |
| **Buffer** | A table of string pieces joined once with `table.concat`, instead of `..` in a loop | 4.04 |
| **C API** | The functions a C program uses to create a Lua state, run code and exchange values through the stack | 6.05 |
| **Capture** | A part of a pattern in brackets; `match` returns what it matched | 4.02 |
| **Character class** | A pattern item for a kind of character, such as `%d` (digit) or `%s` (space) | 4.02 |
| **Chunk** | A piece of Lua code compiled as a unit: a file, or a string given to `load` | 6.04 |
| **Class** | A table holding the methods shared by many objects, used as their metatable with `__index` pointing to itself | 5.03 |
| **Closure** | A function together with the local variables from around it that it uses | 3.03 |
| **Closure object** | An object made of functions sharing captured local variables, which stay private (8.04) |
| **Colon syntax** | `obj:method(x)`, which means `obj.method(obj, x)`; `function T:m()` adds a `self` parameter | 5.03 |
| **Composition** | Building objects out of parts they hold, instead of inheriting from many classes (8.04) |
| **Constructor** | A function, often `new`, that makes and returns a new object | 5.03 |
| **Coroutine** | A function that can pause with `yield` and continue later with `resume` | 6.03 |
| **debug.sethook** | Calls a function on events such as every N instructions; used to stop runaway scripts. (7.01) |
| **Deep copy** | A copy that also copies every table inside, at any depth | 2.05 |
| **Embedding** | Running Lua inside another program, which gives scripts functions of its own | 6.05 |
| **Environment** | The table a chunk uses for its globals: `_G`, or one given to `load` | 6.05 |
| **Ephemeron** | A weak-keyed entry whose value does not keep its key alive. (7.02) |
| **Float** | A number with a fractional part (a 64-bit double); one of the two number subtypes | 1.03 |
| **Floor division** | `//`: division rounded down to a whole number. (7.03) |
| **Frontier** | `%f[set]` in a pattern: the position where the set starts, such as the start of a word | 4.03 |
| **Garbage collector** | The part of Lua that frees tables, strings and functions nothing refers to any more | 6.05 |
| **Generator** | An iterator that produces values on demand, often written with `coroutine.wrap` | 6.03 |
| **Generator function** | A function that returns the next value of a sequence each time it is called, and nil at the end (8.02) |
| **Generic for** | `for vars in iterator do`: a loop that calls an iterator until it returns nil | 6.02 |
| **Global variable** | A variable not declared `local`: a field of the table `_G`, visible everywhere | 3.05 |
| **Higher-order function** | A function that takes or returns another function, such as map or filter | 3.03 |
| **Hole** | A nil in the middle of a list, which makes `#` and `ipairs` unreliable | 2.02 |
| **Inheritance** | A class falling back to another class for anything it does not define itself, through `__index` | 5.04 |
| **Integer** | A whole number (64-bit); one of the two number subtypes | 1.03 |
| **Iterator** | A function that returns the next value(s) each time it is called, and nil at the end | 6.02 |
| **Local variable** | A variable declared with `local`, visible only in its block | 1.02, 3.05 |
| **Long string** | A string between `[[` and `]]`, which can span lines and has no escapes | 1.04 |
| **LuaJIT** | A very fast Lua 5.1 implementation used by LÖVE, OpenResty and Neovim | 6.05 |
| **Luau** | Roblox's language, grown from Lua 5.1 with types and other additions | 6.05 |
| **math.ult** | Compares two integers as unsigned numbers. (7.03) |
| **Memoisation** | Storing the results of a function so repeated calls look them up instead of recomputing | 3.04 |
| **Metamethod** | A function in a metatable with a special name such as `__add` or `__index`, called by Lua for an operation | 5.01 |
| **Metatable** | A table that changes how another table behaves, set with `setmetatable` | 5.01 |
| **Method** | A function stored in a table (or its class) that works on that table, called with a colon | 5.03 |
| **Mixin** | A table of methods copied into a class so unrelated classes can share behaviour (8.04) |
| **Module** | A file that returns a table of functions, loaded with `require` | 5.05 |
| **Multiple results** | Several values returned by one function: `return a, b` | 3.01 |
| **nil** | The value meaning "no value"; also what a missing variable or key holds | 1.02 |
| **os.clock** | The processor time used by the program, for measuring how long code takes (8.05) |
| **Partial application** | Fixing some arguments of a function now and giving the rest later (8.02) |
| **Pattern** | Lua's small language for matching text, used by `find`, `match`, `gmatch` and `gsub` | 4.02 |
| **pcall** | Protected call: runs a function and catches its errors, returning true or false | 6.01 |
| **Polymorphism** | One piece of code working with different kinds of objects, each with its own version of a method | 5.04 |
| **Proxy** | An empty table whose metamethods pass reads and writes on to another table, to watch or block them | 5.02 |
| **Queue with two indexes** | A queue that keeps first and last positions so adding and removing never move other elements (8.01) |
| **Reachable** | Referred to from a global, a live local, an upvalue or another reachable object; unreachable objects can be freed. (7.02) |
| **Record** | A table with named fields describing one thing: `{ name = "Ada", age = 36 }` | 2.03 |
| **Recursion** | A function calling itself on a smaller problem | 3.04 |
| **Sandbox** | An environment that gives untrusted code only the functions chosen for it. (7.01) |
| **self** | The conventional name of the first parameter of a method: the object it works on | 5.03 |
| **Serialisation** | Turning a value into text (or bytes) so it can be saved and loaded back (8.03) |
| **Set** | A table whose keys are the members and whose values are `true` | 2.03 |
| **Set table** | A table whose keys are the members and whose values are true, for fast membership tests (8.01) |
| **Shadowing** | A local with the same name as an outer variable, hiding it inside its block | 3.05 |
| **Shallow copy** | A new table with the same keys and values; tables inside are shared | 2.05 |
| **Stack (C API)** | The list of values a C program and Lua use to pass arguments and results | 6.05 |
| **Stack traceback** | The list of calls that were in progress when an error happened, newest first | 1.01, 6.01 |
| **State** | One complete Lua world created by a host program, with its own globals | 6.05 |
| **string.pack** | Turns values into a string of bytes in an exact binary layout; `string.unpack` reads them back. (7.03) |
| **Table** | Lua's only data structure: keys mapped to values, used as list, dictionary, record, object and module | 2.02 |
| **Tail call** | `return f(args)`, which replaces the current call instead of adding to the stack | 3.04 |
| **To-be-closed variable** | `local x <close> = ...`: its `__close` metamethod runs when the block ends, even on an error | 3.05, 6.04 |
| **Truthy** | Any value except false and nil; 0 and "" are truthy in Lua | 1.05 |
| **Upvalue** | A local variable of an outer function used by an inner function (a closure) | 3.03 |
| **UTF-8** | The text encoding that stores each character as 1 to 4 bytes | 4.05 |
| **Varargs** | `...` in a parameter list: any number of extra arguments | 3.02 |
| **Weak table** | A table whose keys or values (`__mode = "k"` or `"v"`) do not keep their contents alive | 5.02 |
| **yield** | `coroutine.yield`: pause a coroutine and hand values to whoever resumed it | 6.03 |
